newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends down as Pakistan buys Australian.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends down as Pakistan buys Australian.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on disappointment the U.S. did not land a wheat sale to Pakistan, traders said.
"We did none of the Pakistan business," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Export sources said Pakistan bought 225,000 tonnes of wheat from Australia rather than the U.S.

Sources also said Algeria is not tendering for wheat despite reports to the contrary late last week. Also, Bulgaria bought 120,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina and Bangladesh has slated an optional-origin tender for 100,000 tonnes.
Traders said Monday's USDA weekly export inspections report held few surprises for the market.
"Export inspections were pretty much in line with expectations, maybe the wheat number was a little friendly," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA said U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended November 28 totaled 16.367 million bushels, slightly above ttrade expectations for 13.0 to 16.0 million bushels.
Wheat closed 1/4 to 3-1/4 cents lower, with December down 2-3/4 at $3.93-1/4 per bushel.
